collection: NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics construction and angles
note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending. Practical tasks require teacher inspection of the drawing or measurement.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Construct a parallel through a specified point using a compass and straightedge.
questions.prompt: Draw line AB and mark P about 3 cm above it. Using a compass and straightedge, construct a line through P parallel to AB. Leave the arcs visible and explain why the lines are parallel.
questions.answer: A line through P parallel to AB, with construction arcs and a valid parallelism explanation.
questions.explanation: One method is to construct a perpendicular from P to AB, then construct the perpendicular to that new line at P. Both AB and the final line are perpendicular to the same line.

markingGuide.description: Produces the final line through P.
Shows a valid compass-and-straightedge construction, such as two perpendicular constructions or copied corresponding angles.
Justifies parallelism using the construction.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Construct a perpendicular at a specified point on a line.
questions.prompt: Draw a horizontal line and label a point K on it. Use a compass and straightedge to construct a perpendicular through K. Leave the arcs visible. Explain why the first two marks on the line must be equally far from K.
questions.answer: The perpendicular goes through K and the intersection of equal-radius arcs drawn from the two line marks. The marks make K their midpoint.
questions.explanation: Mark equal distances on either side of K. The equal-radius arcs from those marks intersect at a point equidistant from both, so joining it to K draws their perpendicular bisector.

markingGuide.description: Marks points at equal distances on opposite sides of K.
Uses equal-radius arcs from the two marks and joins their intersection to K.
Explains that K is the midpoint.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Construct a 60° angle from a left-pointing baseline.
questions.prompt: Draw ray UV pointing left. Use a protractor to draw ray UW above UV so that the smaller angle VUW is 60°. State how you chose the protractor scale.
questions.answer: Ray UW points up and left. Use the scale whose zero lies along ray UV.
questions.explanation: Centre the protractor on U, align its left-hand zero with UV, mark 60° on that scale and join the mark to U.

markingGuide.description: Uses U as the vertex and UV as the baseline.
Draws and labels an angle of 60° within 2°.
Explains that the chosen scale starts at zero along UV.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Constructing a right angle on a sloping baseline
questions.learningObjective: Construct a 90° angle relative to a sloping ray.
questions.prompt: Draw ray CD sloping upward to the right. Use a protractor to draw ray CE so that turning anticlockwise from CD to CE is a quarter-turn. Label the angle in degrees.
questions.answer: A ray from C at 90° anticlockwise from CD.
questions.explanation: Align the baseline of the protractor with CD. A quarter-turn is 90°, so the second ray is perpendicular to CD and lies on the specified side.

markingGuide.description: Draws CE from C on the anticlockwise side of CD.
Produces an angle within 2° of 90° and labels it 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Construct the midpoint of a segment using intersecting arcs.
questions.prompt: Draw a sloping segment RS about 7 cm long. Without using ruler graduations to locate the midpoint, bisect the segment with a compass and straightedge. Leave arcs visible and label the midpoint M.
questions.answer: M is where the line through the two arc intersections crosses RS.
questions.explanation: Use the same compass radius from R and S, greater than half RS. Both arc intersections are equidistant from R and S, so their joining line crosses RS at its midpoint.

markingGuide.description: Uses equal-radius arcs centred at R and S with two intersections.
Joins the intersections and labels the crossing of RS as M.
Places M so the two halves differ by no more than 2 mm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Measuring an angle from an observed object
questions.learningObjective: Trace and measure an angle using a protractor.
questions.prompt: Open a notebook partway and view it end-on. Copy the directions of its two covers as rays meeting at the hinge. Measure the smaller angle between your traced rays using a protractor and record it in degrees.
questions.answer: Answers vary with the opening. The recorded value should agree with the smaller angle on the pupil’s tracing.
questions.explanation: Centre the protractor at the hinge point on the drawing and align a zero mark with one ray. Read the other ray on that same scale.

markingGuide.description: Shows two rays meeting at a labelled hinge point.
Aligns the protractor centre and baseline with the vertex and one ray.
Records the smaller angle within 2° of the teacher’s measurement of the tracing.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish vertically opposite angles from adjacent supplementary angles.
questions.prompt: Lines AB and CD meet at O, with A and B on opposite sides of O and C and D on opposite sides of O. Angle AOC is 73°. Find BOD and COB and give a reason for each.
questions.answer: BOD is 73° because it is vertically opposite AOC. COB is 107° because it is adjacent to AOC on straight line AB.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles are equal. The angles AOC and COB share OC, and their other sides make a straight line.

markingGuide.description: Finds BOD as 73° and identifies the opposite pair.
Finds COB as 107° and gives the straight-line reason.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Locating corresponding and alternate interior angles
questions.learningObjective: Identify angle pairs by position on a transversal.
questions.prompt: Draw two horizontal parallel lines and a transversal rising from left to right across both. Mark P in the lower-right region at the upper intersection. At the lower intersection, describe the regions containing the angle corresponding to P and the angle alternate interior to P.
questions.answer: The corresponding angle is in the lower-right region. The alternate interior angle is in the upper-left region.
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles occupy the same position at their intersections. Alternate interior angles lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the lower-right region for the corresponding angle.
Identifies the upper-left region for the alternate interior angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Completing the turn around a point
questions.learningObjective: Use a full turn and a right angle to calculate an unknown angle.
questions.prompt: Three rays from a point divide a full turn into three sectors. Two sectors measure 148° and 90°. Find the third angle and say whether it is acute, right or obtuse.
questions.explanation: The sectors total 360°. Subtract 148° and 90° to get 122°, which lies between 90° and 180°.

markingGuide.description: Uses a total of 360°.
Finds 122°.
Classifies the angle as obtuse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.subtopic: Angle of elevation from eye level
questions.learningObjective: Identify the horizontal reference for an angle of elevation.
questions.prompt: From a level school courtyard, Amina looks at the top of a flagpole. Sketch her horizontal line of sight and her sightline to the top. Mark the angle of elevation and explain where its vertex is.
questions.answer: The angle is between the horizontal ray from Amina’s eye towards the pole and the upward ray from her eye to the top. Its vertex is at her eye.
questions.explanation: The two rays share their starting point at the observer. The angle is measured upwards from the horizontal reference.

markingGuide.description: Draws the horizontal and upward rays from the same eye point.
Marks the angle between those rays at Amina’s eye.
